newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/yen ends softer in Europe on Tankan, lira firm.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen ends softer in Europe on Tankan, lira firm.

text.p: The dollar ended softer against the yen in London following unexpected strength in the Bank of Japan's quarterly survey of manaufacturing activity, while the focus in Europe centred on talk of an Italian interest rate cut.
Dollar/yen was almost one yen lower compared with Tuesday's close, although off an early low at 113.30 as the Bank of Japan (BOJ) downplayed the extent of the so-called Tankan's optimism.

The BoJ's diffusion index for big manufacturers, a key gauge of business confidence, rose to plus seven in June from plus two in March, when the previous survey was conducted. Consensus forecasts had been were for fall of 0.5.

"At the end of the day, the Tankan has shown us that the markets are still underestimating the likely rate tightening cycle in Japan and the risks remain for further yen strength," said Mark Geddes, treasury economist at ABN Amro.
At 1505 GMT, the dollar was trading at 113.95/05 compared with 114.78/83 late Tuesday. Dollar/mark closed little changed, meantime, at 1.7248/58 compared with 1.7256/63 late yesterday.

Early dollar/yen losses were pared during the session, however, after a Bank of Japan official pointed out that the Japanese recovery had not strengthened as much as sentiment among the major manufacturers suggested.
The diffusion index for non-major manufacturers, for example, slipped to minus seven in June from minus six in March and the index for small manufacturers improved only slightly.

"There is a big difference between the big blue-chip companies and those supplying domestic demand. That clearly suggests that the domestic economy is not out of the woods," said Jane Edwards, international economist at Lehman Brothers.

The December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures contract moved sharply lower after the Tankan release, however, and is now discounting an interest rate rise of almost half a percentage point by the end of the year.
In Europe, the lira rose to its highest level against the mark since late January on the back of a surge in Italian debt and interest rate markets.

A wave of speculation about a imminent cut in the Bank of Italy's 6.75 percent discount rate and rising optimism about Italy's participation in the first wave of European monetary union pushed the yield spread between 10-year Italian and German government bonds to a record low at 111 basis points.
At 1530 GMT, the lira was trading at 975.65/85 compared with 976.75/05 late Tuesday.
"Italian markets are being boosted from growing confidence in a broad EMU and talk of a near-term rate cut. The lira has taken its cue from the debt markets," said Geddes at ABN Amro.

The rate cut speculation was fuelled by a sharp drop in the Bank of Italy's repurchase rate to 6.26 percent from 6.90 percent previously. Even though monetary sources in Italy cited technical factors as a reason for the sharp drop, government comments showed mounting pressure for an official cuts.
Treasury Minister Carlo Ciampi said low inflation, a strong lira and improving state accounts justified a drop in rates. He said Italy was well placed to start the single currency.

The European Union's monetary committee reviewed Italy's convergence plans for EMU today while the Italian Senate approved a three-year economic plan which sees a budget deficit/output ratio of just 2.8 percent in 1998.
On the other hand, the urgency for a rate cut was underlined earlier by news of a rise in the Italian jobless rate to 12.5 percent in May from 12.4 percent in April.
Sterling/mark suffered an bout of profit-taking after its recent steep rally to five-year highs, but was buoyed later by brisk demand at the Bank of England's latest bond auction.
